Frame_1: The chicken thighs appear mostly intact but are in the process of being prepared. They rest on a plate with a combination of skin and visible underlying muscle tissue. A few distinct characteristics of the thigh can be observed, like the presence of pinkish-white fat and connective tissues. Some parts of the thigh display exposed bone, hinting that the deboning process has commenced.
Frame_2: The chicken thighs are further along in the deboning process. The skin has been partially peeled back, revealing more of the underlying muscle tissue. There are also clear indications of where incisions have been made, particularly around the joints and bone areas. In some portions, the bone appears to be completely removed, leaving behind only the meat and skin.
Frame_3: In this frame, the chicken thighs look significantly more prepared and cleaned up. Most of the bones seem to have been removed, leaving mostly meat. The skin is still attached but appears more neatly arranged around the meat. The overall structure of the thigh has become flatter, suggesting a thorough deboning.
State_change_caption: Over the progression of these three frames, the chicken thighs undergo a clear transformation from their initial state to a fully deboned form. Starting with intact thighs with bones still prominent, the person methodically works to remove the bones, with each frame revealing a stage further along in the deboning process. By the last frame, the thighs appear neatly prepared, with the majority, if not all, of the bones removed and the skin smoothly repositioned over the meat. The transformation showcases the meticulous process of deboning and the stages it entails.
